questions.text: Differentiate f(x) = √(7 – 3x³). You do not need to simplify.
A curve is y = (x² + 3x + 5) cos x. Find the gradient of the tangent at x = 0.
Find the range of x for which y = 3(2x – 7)² + 60 ln x + 12 is decreasing, where x > 0.
Find stationary points and their nature for y = (4x – 3)e^(–4x).
questions.markingGuide: dy/dx = 4e^(–4x)+(4x–3)(–4)e^(–4x) = e^(–4x)(4–16x+12) = e^(–4x)(16–16x). Set=0: 16–16x=0, x=1. d²y/dx²: use product rule. At x=1, check sign change or second derivative. Since e^(–4x)(16–16x) changes from positive to negative at x=1, it is a maximum.

questions.text: A curve is y = 2x – 1/x – 2 ln x, x > 0. It has a point of inflection at P. Find the equation of the tangent at P.
A curve is defined parametrically by x = 3t² + 1 and y = cos t. Find dy/dx.
Displacement s(t) = ln(3t² + 2t + 1), t > 0. Find velocity at t = 1.
Show that y = sin(x²) + cos x is a solution to d²y/dx² + 4x²y = 2cos(x²) + (4x² – 1)cos x.
questions.markingGuide: dy/dx = 2x cos(x²) – sin x. d²y/dx² = 2cos(x²) + 2x·(–sin(x²))·(2x) – cos x = 2cos(x²) – 4x²sin(x²) – cos x. Then d²y/dx² + 4x²y = 2cos(x²) – 4x²sin(x²) – cos x + 4x²(sin(x²) + cos x) = 2cos(x²) – cos x + 4x²cos x = 2cos(x²) + (4x² – 1)cos x. This equals the RHS, so y is a solution.

questions.text: Find the coordinates of the point of inflection on f(x) = (ln x)/x, x > 0.
y = xe^(3x)/(2x + k), k ≠ 0, has a single turning point. Find the value of k and the x-coordinate of the turning point.
questions.markingGuide: Using the quotient rule: dy/dx = [(e^(3x) + 3xe^(3x))(2x + k) – xe^(3x)·2]/(2x + k)² = e^(3x)[(1 + 3x)(2x + k) – 2x]/(2x + k)² = e^(3x)[6x² + 3kx + k]/(2x + k)². Stationary points where 6x² + 3kx + k = 0. Since e^(3x) > 0, for a single turning point the quadratic must have a repeated root: discriminant = (3k)² – 4(6)(k) = 9k² – 24k = 3k(3k – 8) = 0. So k = 0 (rejected) or k = 8/3. With k = 8/3: 6x² + 8x + 8/3 = 0, multiply by 3/2: 9x² + 12x + 4 = 0, i.e. (3x + 2)² = 0, so x = –2/3.

A graph of y = f(x) is shown. It has a sharp corner at x = 3, turning points at x = 0 and x = 5, and the function oscillates for large x.

Find x where f(x) is continuous but not differentiable.
questions.markingGuide: At x = 3, sharp corner: continuous but not differentiable.

questions.text: Find the value(s) of x where f'(x) = 0.
questions.markingGuide: Turning points occur where the gradient is zero, i.e. at x = 0 and x = 5.
The function oscillates as x → ∞, so the limit does not exist.

questions.text: Find the x-values of stationary points on f(x) = (x²–4x+3)/(x²+4x+3). You do not need to determine nature.
questions.markingGuide: f'(x) numerator: (2x–4)(x²+4x+3)–(x²–4x+3)(2x+4). First: 2x³+8x²+6x–4x²–16x–12 = 2x³+4x²–10x–12. Second: 2x³–8x²+6x+4x²–16x+12 = 2x³–4x²–10x+12. Subtract: 8x²–24. Set=0: x²=3, x=±√3.

questions.text:
Sand is poured to form a conical pile. The height always equals the radius. Sand is added at 8 cm³/s. Find dh/dt when h = 4 cm.

Volume of cone = ⅓πr²h.
questions.markingGuide: h=r. V=⅓πh³. dV/dh=πh². dh/dt=(dh/dV)(dV/dt)=(1/(πh²))×8. At h=4: dh/dt=8/(16π)=1/(2π)≈0.159.
